rationale: D7 DEPTH — THE PYTHON-STDLIB CITATION, pinned by evidence class. The Lead extended the committed registry (script/m14/citations.ts) with the `python-stdlib` vocabulary and landed the colon-aware split in the arbiter's namespaceMatchOf, so a python `module:item` import target has a checkable namespace ROOT. This fixture pins the emission: the analyzer declares the root on the edge (`metadata.languageNamespace: [root]`, vocab id `python-stdlib`, subset copied into the analyzer with the id named in the comment) ONLY where the target's root actually is one of those modules — `from typing import Union` publishes `typing:Union` and is cited. The POSITIVE row names the array exactly, because widening it is a reviewable act by the lane (property 2 of the claim design). The NEGATIVE row is the second import: `from django.db import Model` gives target `django.db:Model`, root `django` is NOT in the vocabulary, so NO citation may be emitted — and the reason this is the only negative expressible here is PROPERTY 1 of the namespace claim: the declared list is the SOLE authority, the arbiter never consults the symbol table, so a 'project declares this name' refutation cannot be expressed through this claim at all (that negative belongs to the importedName claim kind, not this fixture — it is stated here rather than faked). A citation that listed a root the target does not have is REFUTED by the arbiter (extFAIL), which is what keeps this mechanism from becoming a blanket excuse; the Lead's gate self-test controls (`pathlib:Path` verifies, `django:Model` refutes) pin the refutation side in the shared instrument.

expectRelationships.note: CITED ROOT: `from typing import Union` — the target root `typing` is in the python-stdlib vocabulary, so the edge declares it and the arbiter verifies the claim (extOK, verifiedBy namespace).
